notes: scan056.N1. The page states (29) for a simplex map preserving the initial vertex: its induced map is called étale and is said to preserve starred and dotted subspaces under pullback. The NB describes the starred part as morally non-singular and the dotted part as singular or boundary, while warning that starred pieces do not form a semi-simplicial space. The final paragraph proposes reconstructing X from open strata and recalls Y closed in X.

scan056.N2. Targeted type and set-operation check: the displayed map has source X_Delta_r and target X_Delta_r-prime, while the equality applies alpha-star to a subset of its target. This is type-consistent as inverse image of a subspace, not as direct image of that subset under the displayed function. If the dotted space is the complement of the starred space, the two equalities are equivalent because f^{-1}(B minus S)=A minus f^{-1}(S) for f:A to B. This conditional elementary check supports the inverse-image interpretation but does not prove the étaleness or preservation theorem from definitions absent on this leaf. No inverse sign or altered index is inserted into the transcription.

scan056.N3. Targeted check of the last example: for Y subset X, the subsets Y and X minus Y are disjoint and their union is X; when Y is closed, X minus Y is open. Thus the written Y=Y-star and X-star=X minus Y give the stated two-piece partition under the open-stratum terminology. This verifies only that explicit example, not a general reconstruction theorem.

scan056.N4. At the first-reader stage, general étaleness, preservation, and the warning that the starred family is not semi-simplicial are carried as background from the author’s setup. The initial-vertex restriction distinguishes preservation under those maps from preservation under all simplex maps, but that restriction alone is not a proof of non-closure. No missing definitions were imported from another page. The subsequent main-reader preservation check and starred-family counterexample are recorded in scan056.N11; étaleness remains unproved here.

scan056.N5. The only page numeral is pale lower-left 55 in another hand. There is no dark authorial page number. H’s section-3 heading is absent; this reader does not infer its location on another leaf.

scan056.N6. After fermée the source has one right parenthesis followed by a comma. Both the outer (où and the inserted (Y subset X opening are retained, so the outer parenthesis is unmatched. C’s extra closer is removed from the count of two physical strokes, not to repair the sentence.

scan056.N11. Root targeted check using the previously read flag construction: a point is (x,i_0<=...<=i_r), and alpha selects i_alpha(0),...,i_alpha(r'). If alpha(0)=0, the first index is unchanged, so the starred condition and its dotted complement pull back exactly as in (29). For failure under other faces, take 0<1 with X_0=Y a nonempty proper closed subset of X_1=X. The starred part of the (0,1) component is all of Y, but the face selecting vertex1 maps it into Y, outside X_1-star=X minus Y. Thus the starred family is not generally preserved. By contrast, a point in a dotted component has a smaller containing index j<i_0, which stays smaller than any selected later vertex; dotted pieces are preserved. This verifies the mathematical importance of the star/dot reading, without using it to override the visible star. Full reasoning is in audit/151_scan056_root_mathematics.md; étaleness is not newly proved by this check.
